children.text: by: Carolina Martinez, Talon Boudreaux, and Jonathan George

Our influencers are Liver King, Shane Gillis, Sydney Sweeney, and our theme is influencer controversy. Controversy is a dispute or disagreement among the public over a sensitive topic or issue which is now more prevalent due to the spread of online content from influencers. Influencers often talk about subjects that divide the population  in order to farm engagement because they know people will give a reaction, and further push their content.

The reason why this is the theme that connects our three influencers together is because they all partially-rely on controversies, whether it be through raunchy humor, suggestive commercials, or intensive lifestyles, that create discourse online that gets people talking and arguing, which ends up helping them gather a larger audience due to the mass circulation online as a result of said-controversies.

Despite the fact all three influencers have very different careers from one another, they all know the saying “all publicity is good publicity” and know how to appeal to the algorithm and right audience so they can continue to be known widely online

The reason why this theme is so important to discuss is because many users online, such as influencers and content creators, use controversies to help get their personal brand and public persona in circulation and in online debate so they’re not quickly forgotten and they stay fresh to viewers. So, with this in mind, it’s easy to see why someone like Sydney Sweeney would market the way she does. Her goal is to stay relevant and appeal to the demographic of her followers. She has learned from being involved in past controversies that discourse helps her become heavily discussed by the public and the media and this helps her gather a larger audience. This also can make companies want to work with and collaborate with her to get their name as heavily discussed.

When it comes to Shane Gillis a little more freedom is given to what he can say. Comedians have the liberty to talk about dark humour. However, this has not stopped Shane from getting in hot water. Shane was fired from SNL only days after being on the cast due to an offensive impersonation of a Chinese accent. This created some turmoil in the Asian community which led to Shane's termination. Shane was able to use this controversy in his stand up comedy which boosted his audience. So even though Shane was faced with a negative controversy, he was able to channel it into something positive for his career.

And why someone like Liver King who uses his controversial living style to build his entire “ancestral” brand, only became more relevant once his authenticity was called into question. When leaked emails proved his physique came from steroid-use rather than his primal lifestyle which ended up leading to his admission of guilt and lying after months of denying, the backlash could’ve ended his career. However, it ended up pushing his name into mainstream conversations far outside his normal fitness audience and into the laps of regular people who never even watched his content prior. Even the fraud lawsuit, which came soon after the backlash that followed, kept him in the news and on everyone’s home page, proving that for Liver King that being in a lie generated much more attention than staying quiet ever could.

Shane Gillis is a man who has many titles. Shane Gillis is a comedian, actor, and podcaster known for his stand-up comedy, Matt and Shane’s Secret Podcast, and the Netflix series Tires. He also has a comedy special on Netflix called Beautiful Dogs. His comedy is where he has found the majority of his success. His style of comedy is usually casual and sarcastic. He also sometimes gets controversial. This can be seen when Saturday Night Live dropped him fom its cast only days after hiring him because old podcast clips of Shane resurfaced where he said inappropriate slurs about Chinese people, and mocked the Chinese accent. These clips faced massive criticism from the Asian community. His style of comedy has helped him create a recognizable personality among his audience. His success has also placed him alongside major celebrities and brands. This  includes Bud Light’s Super Bowl commercial. Collaborations like this convey how Gillis’s influence has expanded past stand-up comedy and into mainstream advertising. Gillis often presents himself as an average guy rather than a traditional celebrity. Sports, drinking, and male friendships regularly appear in his comedy. This makes his partnership with Bud Light intriguing because the company is able to use a personality that Gillis's audience already recognizes instead of having him act like a traditional spokesperson. On January 30, 2026, Gillis posted Bud Light's Super Bowl commercial directly to his Instagram with the caption “New Super Bowl commercial @budlight #SBLX #ad.” The commercial features Gillis alongside Post Malone, a popular musical artist, and Peyton Manning, a famous former football player. Gillis posted the commercial directly to his own followers, so the video works as both entertainment and influencer advertising.

Sydney Sweeney is a very controversial celebrity and influencer. She gained her following through acting in popular movies and tv series, such as The Housemaid, Anyone But You, The White Lotus, and much more. She is best known for her breakout role as Cassie Howard in the Emmy Award winning series, Euphoria. She has used her fame to build a following and social media presence to promote products, work with brands, and create and advertise her own line of lingerie and clothing. Although starting as a celebrity, she has also become an influencer. Sydney Sweeney has many sponsorships with top brands such as American Eagle, Armani Beauty, Kérastase, and Laneige. She even has her own clothing line called Syrn. She promotes these brands by posting photos and reels of her using these beauty products and wearing these clothing brands to influence her viewers. Sweeney is known for her appearance and sex appeal, so she typically promotes fashion and makeup. The idea is that viewers who view Sydney Sweeney as beautiful and desirable will want to be this and take her beauty advice to elevate their own appearance as these products elevate hers. However, many aren’t a fan of Sweeney because they claim she sexualizes herself too much and has a large male audience even though she seems to be marketing brands towards women. A lot of people also dislike that she does not discuss her political views publicly, whether she's a Trump supporter or not. Sweeney's controversy demonstrates the tension between what is or isn't an influencer's obligation for their audience.Despite all this controversy, she still has 25.9 million followers on instagram, and her clothing brand continuously sells out quickly. Even with the hate she receives she is still very successful. Some argue the controversies she’s involved in are intentional to keep herself relevant and heavily discussed by the media. This helps her gather a larger audience.
Johnson, Brian. "@liverking." "[Video of Johnson eating lamb, testicle, and liver while discussing ancestral eating habits.]" TikTok, 31 May 2023.

The TikTok that I'll be analyzing comes from Brian Johnson, known online as Liver King, a fitness and wellness influencer on TikTok and Instagram whose entire persona rests on the claim that he lives an "ancestral" lifestyle, eating raw organ meat, rejecting modern conveniences, and attributing his extreme physique to primal habits alone. That persona is also his business, since nearly every video, including the one I am analyzing, exists to sell his "Ancestral Supplements" line, meaning his authenticity is not just a personality trait but the product itself. What connects him to our group's theme of influencer controversy is that his fame was never built on quiet consistency, it was built on being extreme enough to argue about, and in late 2022, leaked emails revealed that his physique came from steroid use rather than diet, prompting him to publicly admit "I lied" after months of denial. That confession set off a wave of mainstream press coverage, mockery, and a fraud lawsuit from customers who bought his supplements believing his ancestral claims, and rather than disappearing, Liver King became more widely known after the scandal than before it. His career shows how controversy can work in an influencer's favor even when it exposes them as dishonest, since the attention generated by the "I lied" scandal circulated his name and his brand far past his original fitness-niche audience, proving the same "all publicity is good publicity" logic our group identified.
